title: Quantum-enhanced ghost imaging recognition via joint optimization of speckle patterns and quantum network parameters
authors: Yirui Mao, Xiangyu Ge, Yuhang Tu, Anqi Zhang, Le Wang, Shengmei Zhao
abstract: Ghost imaging enables nonlocal image reconstruction and exhibits strong robustness against interference, but achieving high-fidelity recognition at ultra-low sampling rates remains challenging. Quantum machine learning offers a novel approach for efficient feature extraction on noisy medium-scale quantum devices; however, existing methods generally suffer from low recognition accuracy and weak noise resistance. This paper proposes a ghost imaging recognition method based on the simultaneous optimization of speckle patterns and quantum network parameters. By leveraging the mathematical equivalence between classical convolution and speckle-object dot product operations in ghost imaging, a speckle consistency regularization mechanism is introduced to achieve end-to-end joint optimization of optical coding and quantum feature extractors. A parallel 8-qubit quantum circuit employing block coding and a star-shaped entanglement structure is designed to extract higher-order features from bucket signals. Simulation results on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets show that at an ultra-low sampling rate of 1.5625%, the proposed framework achieves recognition accuracies of 90.1% and 81.7%, respectively, representing a 2.6% improvement over classical convolutional neural networks and a maximum improvement of 14.2% over traditional hybrid quantum machine learning models. This method also exhibits strong robustness to quantum noise and has been validated on a real optical ghost imaging system, achieving an average recognition accuracy of 84.8%. These results confirm that the joint optimization of speckle patterns and quantum network parameters provides a reliable and practical solution for low-sampling ghost imaging recognition.
summary: This paper proposes a novel framework for ghost imaging recognition that jointly optimizes the physical speckle patterns and the parameters of a quantum circuit. By integrating a speckle consistency regularization term, the method overcomes the limitations of traditional quantum machine learning approaches at low sampling rates. The results show significant accuracy improvements over classical and existing quantum methods, validating its potential for practical quantum-enhanced imaging.
main_problem: The core challenge is achieving high-fidelity image recognition using ghost imaging, particularly when data sampling rates are extremely low.
main_result: The proposed joint optimization framework significantly improves recognition accuracy (e.g., 90.1% on MNIST at 1.5625% sampling) compared to classical or traditional quantum machine learning baselines.
method: The method jointly optimizes the classical speckle patterns (optical coding) and the parameters of a parameterized quantum circuit (quantum feature extraction) via a regularization mechanism.
model_or_system: The system uses Ghost Imaging (GI) combined with a hardware-efficient variational quantum circuit. The quantum circuit employs a star-shaped entanglement structure and processes input bucket signals encoded via an angle embedding.
key_observables: Recognition accuracy on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets, and the average accuracy measured on a real optical GI system.
important_parameters: Ultra-low sampling rates (e.g., 1.5625%), quantum circuit parameters (Theta), and the regularization strength ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that jointly optimizing the physical speckle patterns and the quantum circuit parameters provides a robust solution superior to fixing one component.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the proposed method, the detailed architecture of the parameterized quantum circuit, and comparison tables/plots showing accuracy improvements over baselines.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the joint optimization methodology involving speckle regularization and quantum circuit design, presents simulation results comparing performance across varying sampling rates, and concludes with validation on a real optical system.
why_interesting: It directly applies quantum computing concepts (variational circuits, entanglement structures) to a quantum optics imaging problem, demonstrating a practical pathway for quantum enhancement in measurement science.
